about.title: La Quinta Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: La Quinta's mix of resorts, golf clubs, retail centers along Highway 111, and residential complexes near Washington Street and Jefferson Street means property owners have a duty to keep walkways, staircases, and common areas reasonably safe. When they don't — a wet tile floor, a cracked parking lot, poor lighting in a stairwell — people get hurt. Under California law, you generally need to show the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn you. That's why documenting the scene matters so much: photos of the hazard, witness names, and store surveillance footage can make or break a claim. LawProactive doesn't represent you directly. Instead, we connect you free of charge with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate what happened, help preserve evidence before it disappears, and explain your options going forward, all on a contingency basis so there's no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Evidence Matter in a California Premises Case

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner had actual or constructive notice of the hazard and didn't address it. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaint records, and inspection history to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many La Quinta businesses and resorts overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to send a preservation request can be the difference between having proof of the hazard and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you were partly distracted or moving quickly when you fell, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows recovery, just reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that reflects the full picture.

items.question: I slipped at a store near Highway 111 in La Quinta. What should I do first?
items.answer: Report the fall to a manager and ask that an incident report be created, then take photos of exactly what caused the fall before it's cleaned up or fixed. Get contact information from any witnesses if possible. Getting medical care documented soon after matters too, even if the injury seems minor at first.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, though claims against a government entity — like a fall on public property — have much shorter notice deadlines, sometimes just six months. Because of that difference, it helps to have a fall reviewed early rather than waiting.

items.question: Do I need a lawyer if the property owner's insurance already offered me a settlement?
items.answer: Insurance companies often make early offers before the full extent of an injury is known, and those offers can undervalue what a claim is actually worth. An independent attorney can review the offer against your medical situation and the evidence at no upfront cost, since these cases are typically handled on contingency.
